turns.thought:
Yes — Airplane Mode being ON is the first thing to fix. It shuts off all the radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), which can also explain why the phone isn't detecting the SIM or showing any signal.

Please do the following on your phone, in this order, and tell me what you see after each step:

1. **Turn Airplane Mode OFF** (swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the airplane icon, or via Settings › Connections). Then check the status bar again — do you now get signal bars and a network type (e.g., 4G/5G)?

2. If the SIM **still** shows as missing after Airplane Mode is off, **power the phone off, remove and reinsert the SIM card, then power it back on.** (I'd suggest this even if the SIM shows active, since "missing" is a common read on a card that isn't seated properly.)

3. Once you have signal, **turn Mobile Data ON** and **turn Data Roaming ON** (Settings › Connections › Mobile Networks › Data Roaming). Data Saver can stay off.

Go ahead and start with step 1, and let me know what the status bar shows afterward. If the SIM is still not detected after re-seating it, let me know — since your device is an eSIM-capable Smartphone Pro Max activated on 2025-02-15, we may need to look at re-provisioning it, and I'll arrange the right help for that if it comes to it.

I hear you — and I'm sorry this has dragged on. The good news is the service side is now fully in order: line active, no suspension, roaming enabled on our side, and 2 GB of extra data applied (valid through your cycle end, 2025-02-28). The remaining checks are all on the phone itself.

Since you're now on 5G with data and roaming on, please run through these in order:

1. **Check APN settings** — Settings › Connections › Mobile Networks › Access Point Names. Look at the MMSC URL field: if it's blank, or the settings show as incorrect, use **Reset to default** (the ⋮ menu). Then **restart your phone** — the reset won't take effect until you reboot.

2. **Check Wi-Fi Calling** — Settings › Connections › Wi-Fi Calling. If it's ON, **turn it off**, then try the picture message again. Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS on some setups when roaming.

3. **Check the messaging app's permissions** — long-press the messaging app › App info › Permissions, and confirm **Storage** (or Photos and videos) and **SMS** are both allowed. If either is denied, allow it.

Please try one picture message after each step, and let me know the result. If MMS still fails after the APN reset and reboot, I'll escalate you to our technical support team directly rather than have you keep troubleshooting — I won't leave you stuck on this.
